info.name: PayPal Orders & Payments API
info.description:
## Overview
This Postman collection covers the complete PayPal Orders v2 + Payments API workflow using PayPal's **free sandbox environment**. No real money is ever processed.

## How to Get Free Sandbox Credentials
1. Go to https://developer.paypal.com and sign in with any PayPal account
2. Navigate to **My Apps & Credentials → REST API apps → Create App**
3. Name your app and click **Create App**
4. Copy the **Sandbox Client ID** and **Client Secret**
5. Go to **Testing Tools → Sandbox Accounts** to find your buyer and seller test accounts

## Setting Up This Collection (Step by Step)

### Step 1 — Create a Postman environment
1. Click **Environments** in the left sidebar → **New**
2. Name it: `PayPal Sandbox`
3. Add these variables:
   - `base_url` → `https://api-m.sandbox.paypal.com`
   - `client_id` → your Sandbox Client ID
   - `client_secret` → your Sandbox Client Secret
   - `access_token` → *(leave blank — auto-filled)*
   - `order_id` → *(leave blank — auto-filled)*
   - `capture_id` → *(leave blank — auto-filled)*
4. Click **Save** and select this environment from the top-right dropdown

### Step 2 — Run requests in order
Run each folder top-to-bottom. Test scripts automatically save IDs and tokens — no manual copy-paste needed.

## Authentication
All requests (except Authentication) use:
```
Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}
```
The token is auto-saved after Step 1 and expires after ~9 hours.

item.name: 1. Authentication
item.description: Exchange your Client ID and Client Secret for an OAuth 2.0 Bearer token. The test script auto-saves the token — all subsequent requests use it automatically.

exec: // Build the Basic Auth header manually from environment variables.
// This is the most reliable method in Postman — avoids the
// Authorization tab being overridden by collection-level auth.
'client_id or client_secret is missing from your environment. ' +
'Open the PayPal Sandbox environment and fill in both values.'
// Base64-encode "clientId:clientSecret" — same as what -u does in cURL
// Step 1: Check HTTP status — show a helpful message on 401
console.error('401 Unauthorized — credentials are wrong or missing.');
console.error('Check that client_id and client_secret are set correctly');
console.error('in your PayPal Sandbox environment and match your');
console.error('Sandbox app at developer.paypal.com → My Apps & Credentials.');
// Step 2: Only proceed if we got a 200
// Step 3: Parse response and validate token
// Step 4: Save token — all subsequent requests use {{access_token}}

urlencoded.description: Required. Always client_credentials for server-to-server calls.

request.description:
Exchanges your Client ID and Client Secret for a Bearer access token.

**How auth works here:** The pre-request script reads `client_id` and `client_secret` from your environment, Base64-encodes them as `clientId:clientSecret`, and injects the `Authorization: Basic ...` header automatically — exactly what cURL's `-u` flag does. This is the most reliable approach in Postman.

**Before running:**
- Open the `PayPal Sandbox` environment
- Set `client_id` → your Sandbox Client ID
- Set `client_secret` → your Sandbox Client Secret
- Both are on your app page at developer.paypal.com → My Apps & Credentials

**After running:**
- `access_token` is auto-saved to your environment
- All subsequent requests pick it up via `{{access_token}}`
- Tokens expire after ~9 hours. Re-run this request to get a fresh one.

item.name: 2. Orders
item.description: Create and manage PayPal orders. An order represents a payment intent that goes through three stages: CREATED → APPROVED (by buyer) → COMPLETED (after capture).

exec: // Guard: ensure we have a token before creating an order
throw new Error('No access_token found. Run Step 1 (Get Access Token) first.');
// Extract and log the approve link for the buyer
console.log('Open this URL in a browser and log in with your sandbox BUYER account to approve.');
console.warn('No approve link found in response.');

header.description: Unique ID for idempotency — prevents duplicate orders on retry

request.description:
Creates a PayPal order in `CREATED` status.

**What happens next:**
1. The test script extracts and logs the **approve URL** from the response `links` array
2. Open that URL in a browser and sign in with your **sandbox BUYER account** (from Testing Tools → Sandbox Accounts) to simulate customer approval
3. After the buyer approves, run the **Capture Order** request to finalise the payment

**Key fields:**
- `intent: CAPTURE` — capture immediately after buyer approval (most common flow)
- `intent: AUTHORIZE` — authorize only; use a separate capture call later
- `PayPal-Request-Id` header — set to a unique UUID for safe retries (Postman auto-generates one)

**order_id is auto-saved** after this request runs successfully.

exec: console.log('Order approved by buyer. Ready to capture. Run Step 3.');
console.log('Buyer has NOT approved yet. Open the approve URL from Step 2.');

request.description:
Retrieves the current status and full details of an order.

**Use this to check if the buyer has approved the order before attempting capture.**

The test script logs a clear message based on the current status:
- `CREATED` — buyer has not approved yet
- `APPROVED` — ready to capture (run Step 3)
- `COMPLETED` — payment already captured

item.name: 3. Capture Payment
item.description: Capture an approved order to finalise the payment and move funds. The order must be in APPROVED status before capture.

exec: // Guard: ensure we have an order_id before attempting capture
throw new Error('No order_id found. Run Step 2 (Create Order) first.');
console.log('Reminder: The buyer must have approved this order first (status = APPROVED).');
// Extract and save the capture ID — needed for refunds

header.description: Unique UUID for idempotent capture — safe to retry on network failure

request.description:
Finalises payment for an approved order and moves funds to the seller.

**Pre-condition:** The order must be in `APPROVED` status. Run **Get Order Details** first to confirm.

**Request body:** An empty JSON object `{}` is sufficient for a standard capture.

**After running:**
- `capture_id` is auto-saved from `purchase_units[0].payments.captures[0].id`
- This capture ID is required to issue a refund in Step 4

**Capture statuses:**
- `COMPLETED` — funds captured successfully
- `DECLINED` — capture rejected by PayPal
- `PENDING` — capture is being reviewed
- `PARTIALLY_REFUNDED` — some amount has been refunded
- `REFUNDED` — fully refunded

item.name: 4. Refunds
item.description: Issue full or partial refunds against a captured payment. Requires the capture_id saved from Step 3.

exec: // Guard: ensure we have a capture_id
throw new Error('No capture_id found. Run Step 3 (Capture Order) first.');

header.description: Unique UUID — prevents duplicate refunds if the request is retried

request.description:
Issues a **partial refund** of $25.00 against the captured payment.

**To issue a full refund:** Remove the `amount` field from the request body entirely — PayPal will refund the full captured amount.

**`note_to_payer`** appears in the buyer's PayPal account transaction history.

**Important:** Include a unique `PayPal-Request-Id` header on every refund request. This prevents duplicate refunds if the request is retried after a network timeout.

**Refund statuses:**
- `COMPLETED` — refund processed
- `PENDING` — refund under review
- `CANCELLED` — refund was cancelled
- `FAILED` — refund failed; contact PayPal support

exec: throw new Error('No capture_id found. Run Step 3 (Capture Order) first.');

request.description: Issues a **full refund** by omitting the `amount` field. PayPal refunds the entire captured amount automatically.

item.name: 5. Webhooks
item.description: Register a URL to receive real-time PayPal event notifications. Useful for payment.capture.completed, refund events, and order lifecycle changes.

request.description:
Registers a URL to receive PayPal event notifications.

**Replace the URL** with your real endpoint before running. For local testing, use a tunnelling tool like [ngrok](https://ngrok.com) to expose localhost:
```
ngrok http 5000
```
Then use the generated `https://xxxx.ngrok.io` URL.

**Supported events registered here:**
- `PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED` — funds captured; fulfil the order
- `PAYMENT.CAPTURE.REFUNDED` — refund processed; update your records
- `CHECKOUT.ORDER.APPROVED` — buyer approved; ready to capture
- `PAYMENT.CAPTURE.DENIED` — capture rejected; notify the buyer

**Verifying webhook signatures:** PayPal signs every event with 5 headers. See the OpenAPI spec (`openapi-paypal.yaml`) for the full Python verification example.
Lists all webhook endpoints registered to your app. Use this to confirm your webhook was created and to retrieve webhook IDs for updates or deletions.
